After six wins from six visits to Anfield for Everton in the WSL era and even quips from their former manager Brian Sørensen in previous campaigns about making Anfield their “training pitch” during their persistent run of victories in this showpiece fixture, Beata Olsson’s early header and Cornelia Kapocs’s late finish were enough to give them a deserved 2-0 victory. Lionel Messi will return a week on Wednesday for his formal farewell in a friendly against Benin, but, before that, Argentina face two games when they will begin to experience a future without the most potent get-out-of-jail-free card football has known. Messi’s international career falls into two distinct halves. There was the first decade when there was a sense that he didn’t quite fit, was somehow insufficiently Argentinian, didn’t care for his country. That was always absurd and can be recognised now as a manifestation of the Argentinian public’s…

pitchfork.title: Northern Exposure
pitchfork.description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the British DJs’ monumental 1996 mix, a virtuosic blend of after-hours grooves and floor-filling intensity that helped to canonize the elusive sound of progressive house.

pitchfork.title: Eternal (Live)
pitchfork.description: A 16-disc box set captures 14 months of live sets from the post-punk titans’ prime. Despite their dour reputation, they prove consistently thrilling on stage, led by Ian Curtis’ whirlwind intensity.

pitchfork.title: Pugnello
pitchfork.description: Exploding its signature blend of noise-punk and dance music to masterful extremes, the Irish band gets louder, rawer, funnier, and more methodical on its exhilarating fourth album.

pitchfork.title: AUDACITY
pitchfork.description: A Beyoncé stan turned pop songwriter, the L.A.-based singer steps out with a major label debut that highlights her versatile vocals, winking humor, and close study of the Top 40.

pitchfork.title: Everyone Gets Everything They Want
pitchfork.description: The Rage Against the Machine guitarist’s towering legacy and sincere political convictions are at painful odds with the sanitized blues-rawk and tedious folk poetry on his new solo album.

pitchfork.title: Happiness Anytime
pitchfork.description: The retro R&B singer surrenders to the groove on a versatile and rhythmic new album that keeps the momentum going without ever really getting anywhere.

pitchfork.title: Bass Persuades
pitchfork.description: Miley Cyrus has a distinctive voice, outsize charisma, and an infamous weird streak, but her short, uninspired new album sounds dated on arrival.

pitchfork.title: No Rest for the Wicked
pitchfork.description: With A&R assistance from Kendrick Lamar, the L.A. rapper shows off his versatility and knack for hooks on an album that effortlessly balances fury, swagger, and introspection.

quietus.title: Living And Dying, Laughing And Crying: the Legacy of Cliff Burton
quietus.description: The undiminished, deep affection for Metallica’s late bassist Cliff Burton reveals a lot about the strength of fanhood in the implacable face of tragedy, says Joel McIver on the 40th anniversary of his death Cliff at his first soundcheck with Metallica at The Stone, San Francisco, 5 March 1983, by Brian Lew I spent six weeks in southern Sweden recently and encountered the spectre of Death in two significant locations. The first was at a rocky beach called Hovs Hallar, near the town of Ängelholm, where the late director Ingmar Bergman shot a couple of apocalyptic scenes from his 1957 film The Seventh Seal. If you know the famous opening scene, you’ll recall that the personification of Death…

quietus.title: Carrying the Fire: Cormac McCarthy’s The Road and the Tradition of Apocalypse
quietus.description: Cormac McCarthy's tenth novel was published 20 years ago. Auden Alsop revisits it and considers the inheritance of assured destruction and how this intersects with parenthood We all know that the world will end. All of this – everything you can see on and behind the screen on which you are reading this piece, and everything you can't – will be lost. We don't know how, when, or why. A nuclear (mis)fire, the eruption of one volcano or another, asteroid impact. When it happens, the how will not matter. Sometime in the ever-nearing future is when; there will be no why. Cormac McCarthy's novel The Road, which turns twenty today, is a simple story, told in ascetic prose, set during the after,...

quietus.title: Animals, Burns and Barns: Trav by Taylor Burns
quietus.description: Taylor Burns' novel Trav is savage and is boldly literary, finds Tristam Vivien Adams Travis Barnes is the protagonist. Taylor Burns is the author. It’s a bildungsroman. The names give it away. The names also resonate with the reading experience on many levels. Author’s name first: Burns. One can be scalded from encountering too cold or too hot a substance. Trav is an intense reading experience. Intense with neutral valence, for the book is by turns frosty and searing. Harrowing and life affirming. Exciting. Stimulating? yes. Pleasant? Joyful? on occasion. Such is life. Welcome to realism. The reading experience is oxymoronic: bleakness is rich and intricate; passion is at times doily…

The theme of next year's SQUARE will be Continuity, and this will explore "the projects that endure,…

It's been split into two parts, with the first part available for streaming now alongside a Ken Ishii…

From there, they worked in isolation with the drafts they had made, before rousay handled the final mixdown of the material for the album. Speaking about the lengths of the tracks that they made, Basta said: "It wasn’t something we specifically…

quietus.title: “Me and You, We Are Not the Same.” Gallows’ Orchestra of Wolves at 20
quietus.description: With their explosive debut album Gallows became the unlikely band to match Sex Pistols' "breach in the pop milieu", but it came with a hefty price tag. Words: Robert Davidson In his 1989 book chronicling the Sex Pistols, Lipstick Traces: A Secret History Of The 20th Century, American music writer Greil Marcus would present one of the greatest questions ever asked in music journalism: “Were the Sex Pistols a major event in history?” Today, we will not ask the same question of hardcore punk band Gallows, who some, initially, saw as a second-coming of the filth and the fury when they erupted in 2006. However, in navigating the Watford band’s short, violent ascendency, a lot of the same…

quietus.title: How Silent Hill 2 Changed Horror Gaming For The 21st Century
quietus.description: To celebrate its 25th birthday, Anna Mahtani unravels how the total assault of Silent Hill 2 – and its roots in modernist literature, alternative music, progressive cinema and modern art – birthed a new era of psychological horror for gamers. Contains spoilers A gentle mist curled around the gravestones as I struggled to find my way out. It was 2021, and I was wandering along the seemingly endless stone wall which separates Cimetière du Père-Lachaise from the rest of Paris. The air resounded with what I assumed was schoolyard glee, but which sounded exactly like screaming. I’d been carried here by an unshakable curiosity, a longing to commune with those already buried. Now, I felt like one…

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Guide to Across the Horizon
aquariumdrunkard.description: What, exactly, is Across the Horizon? It could be accurately described as a podcast, a radio show, an imprint or even a genre; it’s also resulted in a host of compelling collaborations and a series of songs that push at the boundaries of what could be considered ambient music. "It’s like watching a musical community grow in real time," says Bob Holmes. Here’s a look at 10 standout songs from Across the Horizon thus far — music that demonstrates the breadth of the series as a whole.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Dungen :: Vidrig Vår
aquariumdrunkard.description: On the veteran Swedish outfit's most pared down and elegant affair, Vidrig Vår showcases Dungen still operating on a psychedelic wavelength not found elsewhere. Built around bandleader Gustav Ejste's panoramic piano progressions, the ballad-centric record flows with the weightless springtime atmosphere of the band's organically cinematic orbit.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Asher White :: Love Aggregates
aquariumdrunkard.description: Asher White goes maximalist on Love Aggregates , building heavy doses of orchestral power pop from her bedroom. A fragmentary heartbreak album touching on dysphoria, precarious labor, Jerry Garcia, Citi Bikes, and Flatbush in the snow, it transforms intimate falsettos, arpeggiating guitars, and toy piano melodies into a luminous, redemptive vision of love.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Those Were the Days of Miracle and Wonder :: Paul Simon’s Graceland at 40
aquariumdrunkard.description: Paul Simon’s 1986 album Graceland exists in this weird state, an album that eternally evokes 1986, but always sounds so different from other albums of its era. It’s an collection that’s self absorbed, but also so relatable when the listener finds themselves hitting middle age. It brought world music to the forefront, but also presented a misleading picture. It’s a fascinating study in contrast and now, some 40 years later it’s an album we still can’t make up our minds about even as we listen to it for the hundredth time.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Show: SIRIUS/XMU (7pm PDT, Channel 35)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Broadcasting from northeast Los Angeles — the Aquarium Drunkard Show on SIRIUS/XMU, channel 35. 7pm California time, Wednesdays. Subterranean nocturnes dissolve into the horizon. Somewhere between Tokyo, NYC, Caracas and outer space—electric jazz, Japanese fusion, polyrhythms, Rio groove, cosmic funk, library exotica and studio alchemy. 34.1090° N, 118.2334° W

aquariumdrunkard.title: Love :: Four Sail
aquariumdrunkard.description: For many, Forever Changes is where the Love story ends. Whether viewed as a retooled evolution of the band or simply that of Arthur Lee, Four Sail is an essential part of the Love discography. With a driving edge partly recalling the proto-punk energy of Da Capo with the modern hard rock zeitgeist of 1969, Lee's superb new lineup delivers the intentions behind "combining the east and west coast sounds with the European sounds, plus a few of my own ideas".

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Matt Baldwin
aquariumdrunkard.description: This week on the show, guitarist and psychotherapist Matt Baldwin, who is here to teach you How To Play Guitar. OK, not exactly. But Baldwin is the author of ⁠How To Play Guitar⁠, a series of zines that have been collected into a handsome book edition. If you’re just picking up the instrument, well, Baldwin isn’t writing about how to play a C chord or run scales. These aren’t “how to” guides so much as “why to” prompts, stressing intuition over technique, dismissal of music industry norms, and the imperative to hone a singular, personal philosophy regarding the instrument—think Captain Beefheart’s “Ten Commandments of Playing Guitar.” In this talk, we discuss his own guitar journey, the…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Neil Young and the Chrome Hearts :: Second Song
aquariumdrunkard.description: At 80, Neil Young remains gloriously unfinished. Second Song , his latest with the Chrome Hearts, is a weathered, luminous meditation on memory, mortality, love, and the strange passage of time. With shimmering textures, warm harmonies, wandering tempos, and that unmistakably vulnerable voice, Young looks backward without quite letting go of the future. An elegiac, deeply human record from an artist still searching for the song.

As in our sleeping dreams, a sense of infinite possibility stretches before us. That seemingly limitless vista soon disappoints once it is foreshortened into something real and recognizable, such as a place, an environment, a mood, a character, a theme, a genre, or a plot.
